beginner.summary: For ML engineers, data scientists and developers who can run a PyTorch or Hugging Face model but have never compressed one. Covers why quantization matters for memory and decoding speed, FP32, FP16, BF16, INT8 and FP8 number formats, scale and zero-point arithmetic, per-tensor, per-channel and group-wise scales, PTQ compared with QAT, PyTorch dynamic and static INT8, bitsandbytes 8-bit and NF4, torchao weight-only, loading GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints, GGUF and llama-quantize, perplexity and lm-evaluation-harness checks, memory sizing and a small-LLM capstone.
prerequisites: Runs Python 3.10 or later scripts and uses pip in a virtual environment
Has loaded a model with PyTorch or Hugging Face Transformers and generated text or predictions at least once
Has a free Google Colab T4 session or a Linux, macOS or Windows machine with 16 GB RAM, and optionally an NVIDIA GPU with 8 GB or more
outcomes: Calculate scale, zero-point, quantization error and weight memory for INT8, INT4 and FP8 formats by hand and in code
Quantize a small model with PyTorch, bitsandbytes, torchao and llama.cpp and load pre-quantized GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints
Measure perplexity, task accuracy, file size and tokens per second for each variant and compare them in one table
Choose a precision for a given GPU memory budget and defend the choice with measured numbers
